title: Reduction of Probabilistic Chemical Reaction Networks
claim: Reducing a structured model and then compiling it gives the same result as compiling first and reducing the compiled system.
layout: 1 panel, 2x2 square commutative diagram, solid arrows with one dashed arrow
description: A commutative diagram on a white background, with no color or icons. The top row has a calligraphic F on the left and F-prime on the right. A solid horizontal arrow labeled r joins them, and this is the factor-graph retraction. Two solid vertical arrows labeled calligraphic N run down from F and F-prime to Gamma and Gamma-prime on the bottom row. These are the chemical reaction networks compiled from each factor graph. A dashed horizontal arrow labeled N(r) joins Gamma to Gamma-prime. It is the induced CRN reduction, and the dashing marks it as derived. The vertical arrows start with a tick. The eye goes to the top arrow first, then follows the sides down to the dashed arrow. The picture says that the square commutes: reducing at the factor-graph level and then compiling matches compiling and then reducing.
caption: An SP–B retraction r at the factor-graph level induces a CRN reduction N(r) that preserves BP fixed points on surviving variables (Proposition 6.2, Lemma 6.3).
abstract: Programming adaptive behaviors at the cellular level is a long-standing goal that raises the question of how probabilistic computation can be implemented in biochemical systems. Chemical reaction networks (CRNs) provide such a substrate and have been shown to realize probabilistic models, including hidden Markov models and factor graphs, with dynamics reproducing Bayesian inference and belief propagation. However, encoding these algorithms typically requires prohibitively large reaction networks, and classical CRN reduction techniques do not directly apply. By recovering the factor graph structure encoded in Napp--Adams-compiled CRNs, we transport recent factor-graph reduction results to their chemical implementations, obtaining significantly smaller CRNs while preserving the belief-propagation fixed points on surviving variables.
